fixed.explanation: pandas/api/__init__.py never imported the public `internals` submodule, so it only appeared in dir(pandas.api) after something else imported it. The edits import it in the package __init__ and add it to __all__. `pd.api.internals` is then reachable after a bare `import pandas`, and test_api passes when run alone.

query.intent: The pandas.api package __init__ imports only some submodules (extensions, indexers, interchange, types, typing); the test's allowed_api_dirs includes "internals", which only appears in dir(pandas.api) after pandas.api.internals is imported. Either import internals in pandas/api/__init__.py or adjust TestApi.test_api to import it or exclude it from allowed_api_dirs.
query.symptom: TestApi.test_api fails when run in isolation because "internals" is missing from dir(pandas.api) unless pandas.api.internals was previously imported.

history.analysis: pandas/api/__init__.py imports executors, extensions, indexers, interchange, types and typing, but not internals. So "internals" only appears in dir(pd.api) once something else imports it. The test's allowed_api_dirs expects it. Importing internals in the package __init__ (option 1) makes pd.api.internals reachable and fixes the isolated test run.
